questions.questionMarkup:
A person starts typing the numbers from 1 to 1999. He press the keys total ‘n’ number of times.
The value of n is
questions.questionText: A person starts typing the numbers from 1 to 1999. He press the keys total ‘n’ number of times. The value of n is
questions.explanationHtml:
(a)
The number of times he pressed the keys for one digit number = 9
The number of times he pressed the keys for two digit numbers = 90 × 2 = 180
The numbers of times he pressed the keys for three digit numbers = 900 × 3 = 2700
The number of times he pressed the keys for the numbers 1000 to 1999 is 1000 × 4 = 4000
Thus, total number of times the keys are pressed = 6889

questions.questionText: Below is a sentence of which some parts have been jumbled up. Rearrange these parts which are labelled P , Q , R and S to produce the correct sentence. Choose the proper sequence. It would P : that they were quite in the dark Q : about the policy of management R : appear from their statement S : in dealing with the strike The proper sequence should be
questions.explanationHtml:
(b)
“It would appear ...” can be the only coherent beginning of the sentence. Thus the first part
would be R. Since R says “their statement”, sentence P would follow it because it also says, “that they ...”
Thus, option (b) is the correct answer.

questions.questionText: If you are a brisk walker, there is no need to go to a gym. Your neighbourhood can become your gym. You don’t need fancy equipment to get a good exercise either. All you need is a welldesigned pair of shoes. The paragraph best supports the statement that

options.text: walking outdoors provides a better workout than walking indoors.

questions.explanationHtml:
(d)
By stating that brisk walking does not require commute to a gym, the author stresses the
convenience of this form of exercise. The paragraph also states that brisk walking may result in a good workout.
Option (c) is not appropriate. A gym membership can be a good investment for some.
Option (b) is not given in the passage.
Option (a) seems logical but the paragraph does not mention it.
Option (d) is the most appropriate option.

questions.questionMarkup: Which of the following is not an effect of fly ash on cement concrete?
questions.questionText: Which of the following is not an effect of fly ash on cement concrete?

options.html: It improves the resistance of concrete to sulphate attack.
options.text: It improves the resistance of concrete to sulphate attack.

options.html: It reduces the heat of hydration in concrete.
options.text: It reduces the heat of hydration in concrete.

options.html: It increases the permeability of concrete.
options.text: It increases the permeability of concrete.

options.html: It slows the rate of gain of strength in early days.
options.text: It slows the rate of gain of strength in early days.

questions.explanationHtml:
(c)
The permeability of concrete reduces on addition of fly ash to cement. 28 days permeability of
fly-ash-concrete may be three times as that of ordinary concrete but after 6 months it may be less
than 0.25 times. So, it reduces the overall permeability of concrete.

Radiometric resolution – Sensitivity of the system to small changes in the radiation (wavelength).
